Diagnosed T2DM ~3 years ago in India, HTN ~4 years ago; reports inconsistent follow-up since immigrating 8 months ago due to insurance transition. objectives.text: Apply the Nutrition Care Process to conduct a complete remote nutrition assessment, including diet history, anthropometrics, labs, medication effects, and psychosocial/substance use context.

Synthesize assessment data into an accurate PES (Problem, Etiology, Signs/Symptoms) statement reflecting poorly controlled T2DM related to excess carbohydrate/sugar intake, irregular meal timing, and heavy alcohol use.

Develop evidence-based, culturally appropriate nutrition interventions (e.g., carbohydrate counting with Indian vegetarian staples, meal timing strategies, label literacy, budget-conscious grocery guidance) that respect the patient's vegetarian and cultural food preferences.
Integrate medication management considerations into nutrition counseling, recognizing Metformin GI side effects and timing with meals as a barrier to adherence, and coordinating with the care team.

Apply motivational interviewing techniques to explore ambivalence, elicit the patient's own motivations (career, travel, independence), and avoid confrontation around sensitive substance use and sexual health topics.

Identify red-flag findings (significant unintentional weight loss, heavy alcohol use with elevated LFTs, cocaine use, inconsistent condom use, social isolation) that warrant interprofessional referral beyond the scope of nutrition counseling alone.

answerKey.primaryProblem: Unintended weight loss and hyperglycemia in the setting of poorly controlled Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus, with nutrition-related contributors including excessive simple carbohydrate/added sugar intake, irregular meal timing, and heavy alcohol use
differential: Nutrition diagnosis: Excessive carbohydrate intake related to irregular meal patterns and high intake of refined carbohydrates/sweets as evidenced by HbA1c 9.1%, fasting glucose 230 mg/dL, and diet history of large late-night rice/bread portions, sweetened chai, and sugary beverages

Nutrition diagnosis: Inadequate energy intake possibly contributing to unintentional 30 lb (17%) weight loss, though hyperglycemia-driven catabolism and heavy alcohol/substance use are more likely primary drivers than simple caloric restriction

Medical differential (for referring team): new/progressing diabetic complications (consider further workup) vs. catabolic effect of chronic heavy alcohol use vs. undiagnosed thyroid or GI pathology contributing to weight loss - outside RD scope but should be flagged
Alcohol-related hepatocellular injury (elevated ALT/AST/GGT) as a contributing/complicating factor to overall metabolic control and nutrition status
keyFindings: HbA1c 9.1% and fasting glucose 230 mg/dL indicate poorly controlled T2DM
Unintentional weight loss of 30 lbs (~17% body weight) over 6 months despite normal BMI of 22.0 - concerning for underlying metabolic decompensation
Elevated ALT, AST, GGT consistent with alcohol-related liver stress
Diet history reveals irregular meal timing, skipped lunches, large late dinners, high intake of refined carbohydrates (rice, paratha) and added sugars (chai, sweets, occasional soda)
Vegetarian dietary pattern avoiding red meat, relying on dal, paneer, occasional eggs for protein
Poor Metformin adherence due to GI side effects; fair Amlodipine adherence with morning dizziness
Heavy alcohol use: 2-8 drinks per occasion, 2-6 nights/week, escalating with job stress
Smoking ~1/2 pack/day; cocaine use ~1-2 times/month at social events
Inconsistent condom use (~1-2 times/month) with associated STI history on problem list
Limited local social support; lives alone with no family in US; reports loneliness and ambivalence about change
plan: Document findings using ADIME format: Assessment (anthropometrics, labs, diet history, meds, psychosocial), Diagnosis (PES statement), Intervention (education + goal setting), Monitoring/Evaluation plan

Nutrition diagnosis/PES: 'Excessive carbohydrate and added sugar intake related to irregular meal timing and limited nutrition knowledge as evidenced by HbA1c 9.1%, fasting glucose 230 mg/dL, and diet history of large late-night refined-carbohydrate meals and frequent sugary beverages.'

Provide culturally tailored carbohydrate counting/plate method education using familiar vegetarian Indian foods (portion guidance for rice/roti, emphasis on dal/paneer/vegetables, swap white rice for smaller portions or alternatives)
Address meal timing: encourage structured meals/snacks to reduce long fasting gaps and large late-night intake; discuss practical strategies given demanding work schedule
Counsel on reducing added sugar (chai, sweets, soda) with specific, achievable swaps (e.g., less sugar in chai, water/unsweetened options)
Coordinate with PCP regarding Metformin GI side effects (consider extended-release formulation or dose timing adjustment) to improve adherence

Use motivational interviewing to explore ambivalence; link nutrition/behavior change to his stated motivations (career stamina, future travel to India, maintaining independence) rather than confronting directly

Screen and refer: discuss alcohol use pattern and elevated LFTs; refer for substance use evaluation/counseling (alcohol and cocaine); reinforce importance of interprofessional team (PCP, behavioral health, possible social work for support/isolation)
Address sexual health risk reduction briefly and refer back to PCP/sexual health resources given reported inconsistent condom use and STI history

Discuss social isolation and limited support network; provide information on local community resources (South Asian community groups, diabetes support programs, low-cost food resources/food pantries appropriate to dietary pattern)

Set a collaborative, patient-driven SMART goal for next visit (e.g., one specific small change he chooses, such as reducing chai sugar or adding a consistent lunch) rather than imposing a full dietary overhaul
Schedule follow-up telehealth visit in 2-4 weeks to reassess adherence, labs trend, and readiness to change
redFlags: 30 lb (17%) unintentional weight loss in 6 months despite normal BMI - warrants medical workup beyond nutrition alone
Markedly elevated ALT/AST/GGT suggestive of alcohol-related liver injury - needs medical follow-up and possible hepatology/substance use referral

Heavy, escalating alcohol use (up to 6-8 drinks/occasion, several nights/week) with possible withdrawal risk - refer for substance use disorder evaluation, do not advise abrupt cessation without medical supervision
Cocaine use - safety and cardiovascular risk given tachycardia (HR 110) and hypertension; flag for medical/behavioral health follow-up
Inconsistent condom use with history of STI - sexual health risk-reduction counseling and referral back to PCP
Reported social isolation/loneliness in a patient who is ambivalent about change - monitor for mood symptoms, assess for depression/suicidality via appropriate referral
Tachycardia (HR 110) at rest - exceeds expected and should be communicated to medical team, could relate to stimulant use, dehydration from hyperglycemia, or alcohol withdrawal
educationPoints: Explain the relationship between carbohydrate quantity/quality, meal timing, and blood glucose control in accessible, non-judgmental language
Clarify that vegetarian/Indian cuisine can absolutely fit a diabetes-friendly pattern with portion and preparation adjustments - no need to abandon cultural food identity
Teach basic food label literacy (serving size, total carbohydrate, added sugar) relevant to US packaged foods he now encounters
Explain why taking Metformin with food and possible formulation changes may reduce GI side effects, reinforcing coordination with his prescriber rather than independently stopping the medication

Normalize and destigmatize alcohol/substance use disclosure to support honest ongoing conversation; explain the connection between alcohol intake and both liver enzyme elevation and blood sugar control

Validate his autonomy and fears about dependency while gently connecting nutrition changes to his own stated goals (career stamina, travel, independence) using motivational interviewing rather than directive advice

Provide information about accessible community and interprofessional resources (behavioral health, social work, South Asian community support, diabetes self-management programs) without pressuring immediate action

patient.name: Vladko Bareche
patient.appearance: Sitting in what appears to be a small, dimly lit apartment living room, laptop propped on a stack of books. Wearing a wrinkled button-down, visible fatigue under his eyes, speaks in short sentences and often glances off-camera as if distracted by phone notifications. Posture is slightly hunched, arms often crossed.

persona.personality: Quiet, introverted, hardworking, highly creative, guarded about personal life, values dignity and self-reliance
persona.communicationStyle: Brief and reserved; deflects personal or sensitive questions by redirecting to work stress; opens up gradually with patience and non-judgmental approach; uses understatement ('it's not a big deal') to minimize concerning behaviors
persona.emotionalState: Fatigued, mildly anxious beneath a controlled exterior, somewhat defensive when diabetes severity is raised, softens when goals (career, travel, independence) are discussed
persona.background: Grew up in Mumbai in a large extended family where communal meals were central to daily life. Studied film in college, has worked his way up in television production over the past decade, moved to Brooklyn 8 months ago for a producer role on a creative project he's passionate about. Lives alone in a small apartment, works long and unpredictable hours, has not built much of a social circle outside of work colleagues and industry events. Misses home-cooked food and family gatherings from India.

scenario.studentBrief: You are a dietetics student conducting an initial telehealth nutrition assessment for Vladko Bareche, a 31-year-old TV producer recently relocated from Mumbai to Brooklyn, referred by his PCP for poorly controlled Type 2 Diabetes (HbA1c 9.1%). Review the chart before the call. Conduct a nutrition-focused history and assessment, build rapport using motivational interviewing, and begin developing a nutrition diagnosis and culturally appropriate plan. Be alert to barriers beyond diet alone.
scenario.chiefComplaint: Referred for nutrition counseling due to poorly controlled Type 2 Diabetes (HbA1c 9.1%) with recent unintentional weight loss
scenario.openingLine: Hi... yeah, my doctor said I should talk to a dietitian because my blood sugar numbers aren't good. I'm pretty busy, so, however this works.
tasks: Conduct a thorough remote nutrition assessment including 24-hour diet recall, anthropometrics, and relevant labs
Explore medication adherence and side effects as they relate to nutrition and glycemic control
Use motivational interviewing to assess readiness to change and explore barriers (work stress, substance use, cultural food patterns, limited support)
Formulate an accurate PES statement reflecting the nutrition diagnosis
Deliver culturally sensitive, patient-centered education and negotiate one realistic, collaborative goal for follow-up
Recognize red-flag findings warranting interprofessional referral and document the encounter in ADIME format

profile.setting: Telehealth video visit; patient at home in his Brooklyn apartment, dietetics student calling from clinic office
profile.summary: A 31-year-old recently immigrated TV producer with poorly controlled Type 2 Diabetes (HbA1c 9.1%), unintentional 30-lb weight loss, and significant unaddressed substance use (heavy alcohol, smoking, occasional cocaine) and sexual health risk presents for an initial telehealth nutrition assessment. The case teaches students to conduct a full Nutrition Care Process assessment, apply motivational interviewing with a guarded, ambivalent patient, formulate an accurate PES statement, deliver culturally appropriate vegetarian/Indian-cuisine-based education, and recognize red flags requiring interprofessional referral beyond nutrition's scope.
profile.title: Poorly Controlled Type 2 Diabetes with Unintentional Weight Loss in a Recently Immigrated Vegetarian TV Producer
